question: What is the key insight behind hybrid architecture that makes the engineering complexity worthwhile?
options: Hybrid agents are cheaper to run than either approach alone
Most conversations are dominated by simple exchanges that do not need full pipeline power, while a minority require complex tool use or specialized processing
Users prefer agents that switch models mid-conversation
Realtime models are always faster than pipelines
explanation: About 80% of voice interactions are simple exchanges (greetings, confirmations, short questions) that a fast realtime model handles with lower latency. The remaining 20% require heavy lifting (database operations, multi-step tools, specialized STT). Hybrid lets you use the right architecture for each type of interaction.

question: In the fallback pattern, why does the system try multiple realtime providers before falling back to a pipeline rather than going directly to pipeline?
options: Realtime providers offer a better user experience, so the system tries to maintain that experience and only degrades to pipeline when all realtime options are unavailable
Pipelines are more expensive to run
The framework requires at least one realtime attempt
explanation: Realtime models generally provide lower latency and more natural conversation flow. The fallback pattern tries to preserve this quality by attempting multiple realtime providers in priority order. Only when all realtime options fail does it fall back to a pipeline, ensuring the user always gets a working agent even if the experience is slightly different.
